extracted.intended_audience: UPSC aspirants and readers interested in Indian public policy / governance
extracted.subtask_description: Checklist and evaluation criteria for implementing India's Pre-Legislative Consultation Policy (PLCP): what drafts must be published, what accompanying material must be uploaded, timelines, transparency obligations, institutionalisation steps, and monitoring metrics. Focused on assessing whether government departments follow PLCP requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of draft in the public domain for at least 30 days
rubrics_metrics.description: “Whenever the Government makes any law, it must place a draft version of it in the public domain for at least 30 days.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopted in 2014 as part of PLCP. Evaluation: confirm a draft was published publicly prior to introduction and that the public notice period was at least 30 days. Anti-pattern: introducing bills without any prior public draft circulation. The page notes many bills were introduced with no prior consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upload plain-language explanatory note and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: “Along with the draft, a note explaining the law in simple language and justifying the proposal... should be uploaded.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required accompanying material should make the proposal accessible: a simple-language explanation and clear justification of objectives. Evaluation: check for presence, clarity, and accessibility of the explanatory note. Example of good practice: clear summary that non-specialists can understand; anti-pattern: technical-only drafts with no plain-language summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide assessments of financial, environmental and rights impacts and social/financial costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The policy says the note should explain the bill’s financial implication, impact on the environment and fundamental rights, a study on the social and financial costs of the bill, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation: verify the draft package includes (at minimum) financial impact analysis, environmental impact considerations, assessment of effects on fundamental rights, and social/financial cost studies. Guidance implies these are substantive inputs for consultation; missing or perfunctory impact assessments are an implementation weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upload summary of all feedback received on the circulated draft
rubrics_metrics.description: “The respective departments should also upload the summary of all the feedback that they receive on the circulated draft.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency requirement: departments must publish a consolidated summary of submissions and comments. Evaluation: check whether summaries were uploaded, are complete, and indicate how feedback was considered. Anti-pattern: no summary or selective reporting of feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to the 30-day timeline for receipt of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The policy mandated at least a 30-day public comment period; report notes many instances where the 30-day deadline was not met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure compliance with the minimum 30-day window. The page documents non-adherence (e.g., of 74 placed in public domain, at least 40 did not adhere to 30-day deadline). Evaluation: compute which notices met the 30-day minimum and flag shortened/comment windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and publish implementation statistics (compliance tracking)
rubrics_metrics.description: The page cites implementation statistics (e.g., '227 of the 301 bills introduced in Parliament have been presented without any prior consultation' and breakdowns for 16th and 17th Lok Sabha).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy effectiveness requires monitoring. Evaluation: governments or analysts should track counts/percentages of bills with/without prior consultation, adherence to timelines, and publish term-wise breakdowns. Use these metrics to assess poor implementation and trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a statutory or constitutional right to participate in pre-legislative consultations
rubrics_metrics.description: The page states that the absence of a statutory or constitutional right has watered down the policy's effect and that empowering citizens via statutory and constitutional commitment could be a gamechanger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation recommendation: legislative reform to enshrine participation rights. Evaluation: consider whether legal changes have been made to convert PLCP guidance into enforceable rights; absence is a structural shortcoming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate PLCP provisions into executive and parliamentary procedural manuals
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘The effective implementation of the policy requires subsequent amendments in executive procedural guidelines like the Manual of Parliamentary Procedures and Handbook on Writing Cabinet Notes.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationalisation: update formal procedural documents used by ministries and Parliament so PLCP becomes routine practice. Evaluation: check Manuals/Handbooks for explicit PLCP language. The page notes an example where the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs ignored a request from the Ministry of Law and Justice to incorporate PLCP provisions—an anti-pattern of poor inter-departmental follow-through.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require ministers to include an addendum detailing pre-legislative consultation when introducing bills
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation: 'it must be required of ministers while introducing the bill to place an addendum note on the details of the pre-legislative consultation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative transparency measure: evaluation should verify whether bills are accompanied by an addendum describing consultation steps taken, stakeholders engaged, summaries of feedback, and reasons for accepting/rejecting inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutionalise consultation across Cabinet, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Incorporation of pre-legislative consultation in the procedures of the Cabinet, Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha etc. should be prioritised.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System-wide criterion: ensure all key institutions embed PLCP practice so consultation is consistent across decision points. Evaluation: review institutional rules and standing orders of Cabinet/LS/RS for formal PLCP integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use consultations to strengthen democracy and manage stakeholder discontent
rubrics_metrics.description: The policy 'provides a forum for citizens and relevant stakeholders to interact with the policymakers' and consultations can 'enhance transparency, increase accountability' and help manage discontent (examples: farm laws, RTI amendment, transgender act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcome-oriented criterion: assess whether consultations substantively improved stakeholder engagement, reduced conflict, or altered proposals (example: TRAI and net neutrality after consultations). Evaluation: qualitative review of whether feedback resulted in changes or better stakeholder buy-in; anti-pattern: consultation as a box-ticking exercise with no meaningful engagement.
